newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Oct 31.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Oct 31.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Thursday morning:
** Federal police on Wednesday indicted former prime minister P V Narasimha Rao in a vote-buying case, hours after he appeared in a makeshift court in a separate criminal forgery case
Rao became the first former or serving premier to appear in court on criminal charges
** India's enforcement directorate arrested a director and three former officials of the country's biggest cigarette company, ITC Ltd for alleged violation of foreign exchange rules
** The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) has drawn up plans to expand to 80 centres by March 1997 and 150 centres by December 1997, the BSE chief said on Wednesday
The BSE move follows the approval given by the Securities & Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to allow BSE to set up its trading screens across India subject to certain conditions
** The Industrial Finance Corporation of India reduced its maximum lending rate to 19.5 percent
** The Indian rupee INR= opened steady at 35.70/72 per dollar on Thursday. Dealers expect the rupee to trade in a range of 35.68/78 in the day
** On Wednesday, Indian markets suffered sharp losses rocked by rumours the enforcement directorate had arrested top ITC officials
The benchmark 30-share index of the BSE fell 66.96 points, or 2.07 percent, to 3,172.98. The 100-share BSE index lost 25.91 points to 1,414.02
** ITC shares plunged 18.25 rupees, or 5.68 percent, to 303 at the BSE on Wednesday following rumours that top company officials had been arrested by the enforcement directorate

The Finance Ministry said in the evening the enforcement agency arrested a director of the tobacco conglomerate and three former employees on alleged violation of foreign exchange rules in export deals.
** Engineering equipment maker Thermax Ltd reported a 31 percent rise in its first half net profit for 1996/97 (April-March) to 199.2 million rupees against its year-ago period
** HDFC Bank, a subsidiary of Housing Development Finance Corporation posted a net profit of 191.44 million rupees for the six-months ending September 1996 compared to 113.97 million last year
